result.title: Where Rounding Happens Matters: Rounding-Location Alignment Stabilizes LLM Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Reinforcement learning for large language models often uses separate systems for inference and training. Even with identical weights and BF16 tensors, implementation differences can make an intended on-policy update off-policy and destabilize training. Existing remedies align the entire inference and training stacks, change global precision, or modify the learning algorithm. We ask whether aligning selected parts of the execution stack can stabilize BF16 RL while other implementation differences remain. We align training-side rounding locations with inference in three regions---RoPE, SwiGLU, and residual RMSNorm---by retaining selected intermediates in FP32 until their BF16 outputs. Across four Qwen-family models, aligning all three regions prevents the collapse observed under the default BF16 baseline; RoPE-path alignment alone also suffices in the studied runs, despite remaining numerical discrepancies. The interventions keep the inference engine, matrix-multiplication and attention kernels, and learning objective unchanged.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 BF16 强化学习训练中推理与训练系统舍入位置不一致导致 on-policy 更新失配的问题，通过在 RoPE、SwiGLU 与残差 RMSNorm 三处保留 FP32 中间值以对齐训练侧舍入位置，并在四个 Qwen 模型上验证其可避免训练崩溃。
AI.relevance_reason: 方法线索是「只对齐部分执行栈的舍入位置」这一局部精度对齐思路，可供核查 LVR 或 VLM 推理训练的 RL 流程中训练—推理数值错配是否扭曲轨迹监督与贡献分配；但该文不涉及视觉状态或 latent 生成，迁移需自行验证。
